input.quote: 1.8 HDI agrees that it shall promote the Site and Deerskin Products no less favorably than it promotes HDI's
input.rationale: I reviewed every fee, pricing, promotion and exclusivity provision (Section 3 Fees; Payment (p0019-p0022), Section 6 Exclusivity (p0037-p0042), Section 7 Cross-Promotions (p0044-p0046)) and no provision requires the Company to give HDI terms no less favourable than those given to any third party, or to match or extend to HDI any better third-party offer. The only "no less favorably" comparison mechanic in the Agreement runs in our favour: Section 1.8 obliges HDI to promote the Site and Deerskin Products no less favourably than it promotes HDI's own catalog titles, at HDI's cost. That is an MFN-type benefit to the Company and per the playbook is welcome and not redlined. Section 6.1's restriction on the Company participating in similar Internet projects and HDI's exclusive right to the "Deerskin" brand is an exclusivity term, not an MFN, and is properly assessed under the exclusivity rule rather than flagged twice here. The clause therefore sits at the preferred position: no MFN obligation burdens the Company.

mappings.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
